items.stem: Let {N(t) : t ≥ 0} be a homogenous Poisson process with the intensity/rate λ = 2. Let X = N(6) − N(1), Y = N(5) − N(3), W = N(6) − N(5), Z = N(3) − N(1). Then which one of the following options is correct?
items.explanation: Counts on disjoint intervals are independent, and a count on an interval of length L is Poisson(2L). W and Z cover (5, 6] and (1, 3], disjoint, so Cov(W, Z) = 0. Y + Z = N(5) − N(1) is Poisson(2 × 4) = Poisson(8). Y and Z are independent Poisson(4) variables, not equal. X = Z + Y + W, so Cov(X, Y) = Var(Y) = 4.

items.stem: Let {W(t) : t ≥ 0} be a standard Brownian motion. Then E((W(2) + W(3))²) equals ________ (answer in integer).
items.explanation: For standard Brownian motion E(W(s)W(t)) = min(s, t). So E((W(2) + W(3))²) = E(W(2)²) + 2E(W(2)W(3)) + E(W(3)²) = 2 + 2 × 2 + 3 = 9.
items.check: Write W(3) = W(2) + (W(3) − W(2)) with an independent increment: 2W(2) + increment has variance 4 × 2 + 1 = 9.

items.stem: Consider a Markov chain {Xₙ : n = 1, 2, …} with state space S = {1, 2, 3} and transition probability matrix P = [[0, 1/2, 1/2], [1/3, 0, 2/3], [2/5, 3/5, 0]]. Define π = (18/67, 24/67, 25/67). Which of the following options is/are correct?
statements: π is a stationary distribution of P
πᵀ is an eigen vector of Pᵀ
At least one state is transient
items.explanation: Check πP = π column by column; a stationary row vector is a left eigenvector of P, i.e. an eigenvector of Pᵀ. Two-step probabilities come from P², and a finite irreducible chain has no transient states.

B.why: True: πP = π transposes to Pᵀπᵀ = πᵀ, so πᵀ is an eigenvector of Pᵀ with eigenvalue 1.

C.why: True: the two-step return probability is P²₁₁ = (1/2)(1/3) + (1/2)(2/5) = 1/6 + 1/5 = 11/30.

D.why: False: every state reaches every other, so the finite chain is irreducible and all states are recurrent.
